title: Wild bets and PR
purpose: When a bold bet, a press hit, a partnership or a public problem is in play, open Wild bets and PR to see what it cost, what it brought and when to stop, so a big swing never quietly sinks the quarter.
fires: The founder's gut on bold ideas, the PR agency's clipping report, the partnership judged on reach, and the crisis handled in a panicked group chat.
not_for: A store that has not fixed its basic ads, site and service, or has no spare cash for a bet it could lose; and anyone who wants to buy press as a sales channel.

jobs.job: When a bold bet has run for weeks and the money keeps going out, show me what it has cost against its limit and what it has brought, so I stop it before it eats the quarter
jobs.circumstance: the second month of the quarter, the pop-up and influencer box project is $38,000 in, no end date was set, and it is the founder's own idea

progress.functional: spend to date against the limit, what it brought back, and the days left to its read date
progress.emotional: stop the sunk cost dread; be able to call it early without shame
progress.social: face a partner or co-founder with a number and a clear call, not an excuse

jobs.hire_today: the founder's gut and the bank balance; nobody tracks a bet as one line of cost and return
jobs.fire: letting the bet run until someone notices the cash is short

forces.push: cash drains quietly and the quarter's plan is at risk
forces.pull: one line per bet: spent, limit, brought, days left, and a stop or keep call
forces.habit: stopping feels like admitting defeat
forces.anxiety: what if it was just about to work

jobs.little_hire: weekly while any bet is live, and the day a bet's spend jumps

watch.metric: spend to date on each live bet against its limit, and total bet spend as a share of quarter gross profit
watch.source: brand brain (bet log) and accounting feed

drives.metric: contribution margin, quarter to date

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1 bet has spent $38,000 with no limit. After: every bet stops at its limit; total bet spend stays under 10 percent of the quarter's gross profit.
jobs.not_for: a store with no spare cash, which should not be running bets at all

jobs.job: When a bad review or post about us is spreading, tell me fast how big it is and give me a first reply I can approve, so it stops in hours, not weeks
jobs.circumstance: Saturday, a video about a broken product has 400,000 views, comments are filling up, the founder is at a family lunch

progress.functional: how big it is, how fast it is growing, what is true in it, and a drafted reply
progress.emotional: stop the panic and the urge to fire off a reply from the table
progress.social: be seen to respond fairly and fast by customers, press and the team

jobs.hire_today: the founder's phone and a group chat; a PR agency on call if they have one
jobs.fire: the panicked group chat and the 2am reply

forces.push: sales and trust fall every hour it runs
forces.pull: size, tone and a drafted holding reply within 1 hour, plus the fix for the customer
forces.habit: say nothing and hope it passes
forces.anxiety: what if our reply makes it worse

jobs.little_hire: any spike in mentions or 1 star reviews, and a quiet daily check

watch.metric: hours from a negative spike to an approved public reply
watch.source: social mentions and review platform

drives.metric: review rating, 30 day, and conversion rate in the spike week

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the first reply came 2 days later. After: an approved reply within 3 hours and the customer's refund sent the same day.
jobs.not_for: a brand with no public following, where one review rarely spreads

jobs.job: When a press piece sends a wave of visitors and no orders, tell me why and what to fix fast, so the next hit sells
jobs.circumstance: the morning after a feature in a big gift guide, 9,000 visits and 11 orders, the PR agency is celebrating

progress.functional: see where press visitors dropped off and what the page they landed on lacked
progress.emotional: turn the let-down into a fix
progress.social: judge the PR agency on orders, not logos

jobs.hire_today: the PR agency's clipping report; GA4 if someone thinks to check
jobs.fire: the clipping report as proof of value

forces.push: the retainer is $5,000 a month and orders are flat
forces.pull: visits, orders and cost per order for each piece, and the fix for the landing page
forces.habit: press is 'brand', so it is not judged on sales
forces.anxiety: what if press only pays off months later

jobs.little_hire: each time a piece runs, and monthly when the PR invoice lands

watch.metric: visits, orders and conversion rate from each press piece, 14 days
watch.source: GA4 referral data and store orders

drives.metric: new customers from earned media, per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 9,000 visits and 11 orders; the link went to the home page. After: the next piece lands on a matched page and converts at 1.5 percent.
jobs.not_for: a brand that wants press only for credibility and will not judge it on orders

jobs.job: When a bold idea gets a yes, write down the most it can cost, the stop rule and the read date before any money moves, so a bet can never become a crisis
jobs.circumstance: Friday, the founder and a partner agree on a surprise gift box for 2,000 customers; the order to the supplier goes out Monday

progress.functional: a limit on money, a stop rule, a date to judge it and a group to compare with, agreed before launch
progress.emotional: the calm of a known worst case
progress.social: give a partner or investor a bet they can back

jobs.hire_today: a handshake and a rough number in a chat; often nothing, because it feels like it kills the fun
jobs.fire: launching on excitement and a rough number

forces.push: a past bet ran over and hurt cash
forces.pull: a short sheet signed before money moves: most it can lose, stop rule, read date
forces.habit: we are a scrappy brand, we just try things
forces.anxiety: what if the rules make us too slow to catch the moment

watch.metric: share of bets launched with a cost limit, stop rule, read date and comparison group on file
watch.source: brand brain (bet log)

drives.metric: dollars spent on bets beyond their limits, per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1 of 3 live bets has a limit and none has a stop rule. After: nothing launches without all 4; the worst case across the 3 is $6,000.
jobs.not_for: a small, cheap test under a few hundred dollars that needs no paperwork

jobs.job: When a partnership or collab ends, tell me the orders, new customers and cost per order it brought next to paid ads, so I renew only the ones that paid
jobs.circumstance: a collab with a coffee brand ran 3 months, both sides posted, nobody set a code, and their renewal email just arrived

progress.functional: orders and new customers from the partner, and what each cost against paid ads
progress.emotional: stop the vague feeling that it was 'good for the brand'
progress.social: tell the partner yes or no with numbers, and keep the relationship

jobs.hire_today: nothing; partnerships are judged on reach and feel because nobody set up a way to count orders
jobs.fire: judging the partnership on likes and a friendly call

forces.push: the next partnership fee is due and nobody knows if the last one paid
forces.pull: a code or link set up at the start and a cost per order at the end
forces.habit: partnerships are relationships, not ads
forces.anxiety: what if the count misses buyers who saw it and bought later

jobs.little_hire: at the start of each partnership, monthly while live, and at renewal

watch.metric: orders and new customers from the partner's code or tracked link, 30 days, and cost per order
watch.source: brand brain (press and partner log) and store orders

drives.metric: blended cost per new customer, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $12,000 in fees and product with no count. After: the next one has a code; 140 orders at $34 each against $48 on paid social; renewed.
jobs.not_for: a partnership done for a cause, where orders are not the goal

jobs.job: When a big sale is on the calendar, test a gift, a bundle or a price hold against the usual discount, so we keep the sales and more of the margin
jobs.circumstance: October, the Black Friday plan is 30 percent off everything again; last year's margin was thin

progress.functional: profit from the sale under the new offer compared with the old discount
progress.emotional: stop the dread of training buyers to wait for sales
progress.social: try something bold without betting the whole peak

jobs.hire_today: the same sale as last year, set by habit or the agency

forces.push: deep discounts cut margin and train buyers to wait
forces.pull: a bounded test on part of the list, with profit compared
forces.habit: everyone discounts on Black Friday
forces.anxiety: what if we lose the peak

watch.metric: profit after discounts during the sale window, test group versus discount group
watch.source: store orders and brand brain (bet log)

drives.metric: gross margin, quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 30 percent off, 22 percent margin. After: gift with purchase on half the list, 34 percent margin, same orders.
jobs.not_for: a store that does not run sales

jobs.job: When I want to launch a new product, sell it on pre-order or in a small drop first, so I buy stock for real demand, not a hunch
jobs.circumstance: the supplier needs a 3,000 unit order for a new colour; the founder loves it

progress.functional: real orders before the big stock buy
progress.emotional: sleep without a warehouse of unsold stock
progress.social: show a partner the buy is backed by orders

jobs.hire_today: gut, a poll of followers, or a friend's view

forces.push: past launches left stock for a year
forces.pull: pre-orders against a target set before launch
forces.habit: we buy stock and then sell
forces.anxiety: what if pre-orders put buyers off

jobs.little_hire: before each new product or colour

watch.metric: pre-orders or drop sales versus the target set before launch, in the window
watch.source: store orders and brand brain (bet log)

drives.metric: days of stock on new products at 90 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3,000 units bought, 1,100 sold in a year. After: 400 pre-orders, a buy of 1,200 that sells through in 4 months.
jobs.not_for: a product that must be in stock to sell, like a daily need

jobs.job: When a bet reaches its read date, tell me if it beat a group that did not get it, so I scale real wins and stop the ones that only rode a good month
jobs.circumstance: the handwritten note bet reached its 60 day date; repeat orders are up, but so is the whole store

progress.functional: the gain against a comparable group left out, not against last month
progress.emotional: trust the call to scale or stop
progress.social: defend the call to a partner who liked the idea

jobs.hire_today: nothing, or a before and after that flatters the bet

forces.push: bets get scaled on luck
forces.pull: gain versus a left-out group, in one number
forces.habit: if sales went up, it worked
forces.anxiety: what if the left-out group lost sales we could have made

watch.metric: gain on the bet's named metric versus the left-out group, at the read date
watch.source: brand brain (bet log)

drives.metric: gross profit per customer reached

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the note bet looks like plus 20 percent. After: plus 4 percent over the left-out group; kept but not scaled.
jobs.not_for: a one-off stunt with no way to hold a group back

jobs.job: When a post goes viral for good reasons, make sure the site, stock and ads are ready to catch it within hours, so the spike turns into orders
jobs.circumstance: a customer's video about us hit 1 million views overnight; the linked product is out of stock in 2 sizes

progress.functional: stock, the landing page and ads lined up while the wave lasts, usually 48 hours
progress.emotional: turn luck into sales, not regret
progress.social: look ready to the new crowd

jobs.hire_today: nothing; nobody plans for a spike they cannot predict, so the team reacts days late
jobs.fire: reacting 3 days late, after the wave has passed

forces.push: the wave lasts about 48 hours and then is gone
forces.pull: a short list of moves to make in the first hour
forces.habit: we react when someone happens to notice
forces.anxiety: what if we overbuy on a spike

jobs.little_hire: any spike in mentions or traffic

watch.metric: orders in the 72 hours after a spike versus a normal 72 hours
watch.source: store orders and social mentions

drives.metric: new customers per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1 million views, 60 orders, 2 sizes sold out. After: the next spike, 600 orders and a waitlist.
jobs.not_for: a brand with no social presence

jobs.job: When the quarter's plan is set, fix how much in total we can lose on bold bets, so no run of small bets puts cash at risk
jobs.circumstance: quarter planning; 5 small bets each look cheap on their own

progress.functional: one total limit for all bets in the quarter, tied to profit
progress.emotional: the calm of a known worst case for the quarter
progress.social: give a partner or investor one clear number

jobs.hire_today: nothing; each bet is approved on its own, so nobody adds them up
jobs.fire: approving bets one by one with no running total

forces.push: 5 small bets add up to a big hole in cash
forces.pull: one quarterly limit tied to profit
forces.habit: each bet is small, so none feels risky
forces.anxiety: what if a great bet comes after the limit is used

watch.metric: total bet spend this quarter as a share of profit after ads
watch.source: brand brain (bet log) and accounting feed

drives.metric: cash on hand at quarter end

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 5 bets spent $41,000, 30 percent of quarter profit. After: capped at 10 percent.
jobs.not_for: a store with no bets planned

jobs.job: When the top 2 percent of buyers drive a large share of profit, treat them as insiders and see if they buy more than similar buyers left out, so we keep and grow them
jobs.circumstance: the founder notices 300 customers bought 5 or more times; they get the same emails as everyone

progress.functional: an insider group with a real reason to feel special, measured against a left-out group
progress.emotional: the warmth of knowing our best customers feel seen
progress.social: turn best customers into people who talk about us

jobs.hire_today: nothing, or a points app that treats a 1-time buyer and a 10-time buyer the same, because hand-picking feels like too much work

forces.push: best customers drift to rivals without anyone noticing
forces.pull: a small, hand-picked group and a clear read
forces.habit: the loyalty app already handles loyalty
forces.anxiety: what if the program costs more than it brings

watch.metric: repeat purchase rate of the inner circle versus similar buyers left out, 90 days
watch.source: store orders and brand brain (bet log)

drives.metric: gross profit per top customer, 12 months

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: top buyers get the same emails. After: insiders buy 18 percent more than the left-out group.
jobs.not_for: a store with fewer than 500 repeat buyers

jobs.job: When the PR agency's retainer is up for renewal, show the visits, links and orders from each placement over the term, so I renew on results
jobs.circumstance: month 6 of a $5,000 a month PR retainer; the report is a list of logos

progress.functional: what each placement brought
progress.emotional: stop wondering what the retainer buys
progress.social: hold the PR agency to a number at renewal

jobs.hire_today: the agency's clipping report

forces.push: the fee is $30,000 so far and the result is unclear
forces.pull: each placement with visits, links and orders
forces.habit: everyone says press is hard to measure
forces.anxiety: what if good press pays off later

watch.metric: visits, new linking sites and orders from each placement over the retainer term
watch.source: brand brain (press and partner log), GA4 and store orders

drives.metric: cost per new customer from earned media

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $30,000 spent, 14 logos. After: 3 placements brought 80 percent of the visits; the agency is moved to a per-story fee.
jobs.not_for: a brand with no PR agency

jobs.job: When 6 bold ideas are on the table and there is money for 1, show me the cost, the downside and the habit each breaks, so I back the one with the best odds
jobs.circumstance: quarter planning; the team pitches a pop-up, a mystery box, a no-ads week, a collab, a stunt and a founder podcast

progress.functional: each idea's cost, worst case and why it could work
progress.emotional: stop picking by excitement and regretting it at quarter end
progress.social: pick fairly between team ideas

jobs.hire_today: the founder's gut, or the idea with the loudest champion

forces.push: the wrong bet uses the whole quarter's budget
forces.pull: a side by side with cost, downside and odds
forces.habit: the founder picks the idea they like most
forces.anxiety: what if the best idea looks weak on paper

watch.metric: bets chosen with cost, downside and named metric written, per quarter
watch.source: brand brain (bet log)

drives.metric: share of bets that beat their read point bar

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the pop-up picked by excitement lost $15,000. After: the mystery box picked on odds, plus $6,000 in profit.
jobs.not_for: a store with no bet budget

jobs.job: When an event or pop-up is offered, count the orders and sign-ups it brings at its full cost, so I pick the next event on cost per customer
jobs.circumstance: a market asks $4,000 for a stall; last year's events were judged on 'buzz'

progress.functional: orders and sign-ups counted with an event code, against the full cost of stall, stock, travel and team days
progress.emotional: no more tired weekends that quietly lost money
progress.social: tell the team which events pay

jobs.hire_today: gut and the buzz on the day; nobody sets a code, so nothing is counted
jobs.fire: buzz as the measure of an event

forces.push: events eat weekends, stock and cash
forces.pull: a code per event and a cost per customer
forces.habit: events are brand building, not sales
forces.anxiety: what if the buyers come later online

watch.metric: orders and email sign-ups with the event code within 14 days, and cost per new customer
watch.source: store orders and brand brain (press and partner log)

drives.metric: new customers per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 events, results unknown. After: 1 event at $22 a customer kept, 3 dropped.
jobs.not_for: a brand with no in-person buyers

jobs.job: When we know a problem is coming, like a recall, a delay or a price rise, draft what we will say before customers find out, so we tell the story first
jobs.circumstance: the supplier says the next shipment is 5 weeks late; 800 pre-orders are waiting

progress.functional: a message ready and sent to the affected customers before complaints start
progress.emotional: calm instead of dread about the inbox
progress.social: look honest and in control to buyers

jobs.hire_today: the founder writes it when the complaints start; before that, nothing, because nobody wants to give bad news early

forces.push: silence turns into angry posts and chargebacks
forces.pull: a draft ready the day we know, with the offer to cancel or wait
forces.habit: wait and hope the problem resolves itself
forces.anxiety: what if telling people early loses orders

watch.metric: days from knowing a problem to telling affected customers
watch.source: brand brain (issue log) and email tool

drives.metric: refund and cancel rate on affected orders

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: customers found out from tracking. After: an email the same day; 3 percent cancelled, not 15.
jobs.not_for: a brand with no known issues ahead

jobs.job: When ambassadors need tasks, content checks and follow-up every week, run it on a routine and count each one's orders, so the program does not eat my week
jobs.circumstance: 40 ambassadors, a dozen DMs a night, posts waiting for approval, and the founder answering them all after dinner

progress.functional: a weekly routine for tasks and checks, and orders counted per ambassador
progress.emotional: get evenings back without feeling the program is slipping
progress.social: keep ambassadors feeling valued and seen by the brand

jobs.hire_today: the founder at night, or a part-time community lead paid by the hour
jobs.fire: the founder's evenings as the operating system

forces.push: the program eats 8 hours a week and nobody knows what it earns
forces.pull: a set weekly rhythm and a list of who brings orders
forces.habit: the founder is the face of the brand, so the founder answers
forces.anxiety: what if ambassadors feel the personal touch is gone

jobs.little_hire: weekly, and the day posts pass their review deadline

watch.metric: orders from ambassador codes per month, and posts waiting past the review deadline
watch.source: store orders and brand brain (press and partner log)

drives.metric: cost per order from ambassadors, product and fees included

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 8 founder hours a week, orders unknown. After: 2 hours; 6 of 40 ambassadors bring 70 percent of orders and get more support.
jobs.not_for: a brand with no ambassador program, or one with under 10 people the founder can handle personally

jobs.job: When customers say they love us but referrals stay flat, find a reason worth telling a friend and count the orders, so word of mouth becomes a channel
jobs.circumstance: reviews average 4.8 stars, yet the $10 off referral code brings 1 percent of orders and nobody has touched it in 2 years

progress.functional: a referral reason people actually use, and its share of orders
progress.emotional: feel the goodwill turn into growth
progress.social: give customers something they are proud to share

jobs.hire_today: a referral app with a plain discount, set up once and left alone
jobs.fire: the plain discount code nobody talks about

forces.push: growth leans on paid ads that cost more each quarter
forces.pull: a reason to share that fits the brand, with orders counted
forces.habit: the app is installed, so referrals are handled
forces.anxiety: what if a bigger reward costs more than it brings

watch.metric: share of orders from a referral code or link, monthly
watch.source: store orders

drives.metric: blended cost per new customer, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1 percent of orders from referrals. After: 4 percent after a gift for both friends, at half the cost of a paid customer.
jobs.not_for: a store with low repeat buying and weak reviews; fix the product and service first

jobs.job: When we plan a surprise gift or VIP touch, leave out customers with an open complaint and check service is sound, so the gesture does not land on an angry customer
jobs.circumstance: a gift box is going to the top 300 buyers next week; 12 of them have open tickets about late orders

progress.functional: an exclusion list of unhappy customers and a check that replies are on time
progress.emotional: no awkward backlash from a gift that feels like a slap
progress.social: look thoughtful, not out of touch

jobs.hire_today: nothing; gift lists are built from spend alone because support data sits in another tool

forces.push: a gift to an angry customer can end up in a public post
forces.pull: open issues left out every time, and a service check before launch
forces.habit: top spenders are the top list
forces.anxiety: what if we leave out someone who would have loved it

watch.metric: customers with an open issue included in a bet
watch.source: help desk and brand brain (bet log)

drives.metric: first reply time, 7 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 12 customers with open complaints got a gift. After: 0, and their issues fixed first.
jobs.not_for: a brand not running any delight or VIP bets

jobs.job: When an ambassador or partner does something public that clashes with us, know within a day and have a way out, so their problem does not become ours
jobs.circumstance: a paid creator posted something that angers our buyers; customers tag us in the comments

progress.functional: fast notice and a written way out
progress.emotional: no dread of being tied to someone else's mess
progress.social: protect the brand in public

jobs.hire_today: nothing until customers tell us, because nobody watches partners after signing

forces.push: their problem becomes ours within hours
forces.pull: a watch on partners and an exit clause ready
forces.habit: trust partners once signed
forces.anxiety: what if we overreact to a small thing

jobs.little_hire: ongoing, and daily while a partner is live

watch.metric: hours from a partner's public problem to our response
watch.source: brand brain (press and partner log) and social mentions

drives.metric: review rating, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 days to notice. After: 1 day, and the exit clause used.
jobs.not_for: a brand with no partners or ambassadors

jobs.job: When a partner, creator or licensee wants to sign, check their past, their buyers and any clash with our category, so they cannot embarrass us later
jobs.circumstance: a creator with 2 million followers offers a paid collab; the contract is due Friday and nobody has read their old posts

progress.functional: a check of their past posts, their audience and any clash with our products
progress.emotional: no fear of a scandal landing on us later
progress.social: protect the brand's name with buyers and retailers

jobs.hire_today: a quick scroll of their profile; often nothing, because the deal feels too good to slow down
jobs.fire: signing on excitement and follower count

forces.push: one partner scandal can hit sales for months
forces.pull: a short check before any signature, with a clear pass or flag
forces.habit: big names sell, so we sign fast
forces.anxiety: what if the check turns down a great deal

watch.metric: partners approved with an open reputation flag
watch.source: brand brain (press and partner log)

drives.metric: review rating, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 0 checks before 5 deals. After: 1 of 5 turned down for old posts that clashed with our buyers.
jobs.not_for: a small one-off product gift with no contract or paid fee

jobs.job: When a bet works for 50 customers, grow it in steps with a check at each step, so it does not break at 5,000 in cost or team hours
jobs.circumstance: the founder video bet worked for 50 customers; the plan is to send 5,000 next month with the same 2 person team

progress.functional: growth in steps with a pass mark on profit and hours at each
progress.emotional: no fear the bet breaks when it gets big
progress.social: protect the team from a load they cannot carry

jobs.hire_today: gut, and a big jump once something works
jobs.fire: the big jump straight to full size

forces.push: a big jump costs cash and burns the team out
forces.pull: a step plan with a pass mark at each step
forces.habit: when it works, go big
forces.anxiety: what if the steps are too slow and the moment passes

jobs.little_hire: at each step of a growing bet

watch.metric: gross profit per customer reached, at each stage
watch.source: brand brain (bet log)

drives.metric: team hours per 100 customers reached

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: planned jump from 50 to 5,000. After: 500, then 2,000; profit per customer held and hours stayed inside the team's week.
jobs.not_for: a one-off bet that will not be repeated

jobs.job: When podcast and panel invites pile up, pick the ones where our buyers listen and count visits from each, so my time on stage sells
jobs.circumstance: the founder did 6 podcasts last quarter, each took half a day, and nobody knows if any sent a buyer

progress.functional: appearances picked on audience fit, each with a code or link to count
progress.emotional: stop giving time with nothing to show
progress.social: build the founder's name where buyers and press listen

jobs.hire_today: saying yes to everyone, or a PR agency that books by volume

forces.push: the founder's time is the scarcest thing in the business
forces.pull: a fit check before yes, and a count after
forces.habit: any exposure is good exposure
forces.anxiety: what if the value is slow and the count misses it

watch.metric: founder appearances per quarter and visits from each, 30 days
watch.source: brand brain (press and partner log) and GA4

drives.metric: new customers from founder appearances, per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 6 podcasts, 0 counted. After: 3 podcasts with a code; 1 brought 90 orders, 2 brought under 5.
jobs.not_for: a founder who does not want a public role

jobs.job: When I want to try a new country or a new sales channel, run it as a small capped test through a platform that already exists, so I learn demand without building a new business
jobs.circumstance: a distributor offers the UK; the founder is tempted to set up a local store and warehouse

progress.functional: a small, capped read on demand before any build
progress.emotional: no fear of a costly failure abroad
progress.social: show a partner the move is backed by real orders

jobs.hire_today: a big launch on hope, or nothing, because the build feels too big to start
jobs.fire: the big build as the first step

forces.push: new markets are slow and costly to enter
forces.pull: a small capped test through a marketplace or partner
forces.habit: all in or nothing
forces.anxiety: what if the test is too small to read

jobs.little_hire: each new market or channel idea

watch.metric: orders and profit per order in the test market, 90 days
watch.source: marketplace reports and brand brain (bet log)

drives.metric: revenue from new markets, per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a $40,000 launch planned. After: a $5,000 test with 200 orders; the next step approved on the numbers.
jobs.not_for: a store that cannot yet ship or serve customers abroad

jobs.job: When a founder friend says a stunt tripled their sales, test it small on our own customers first, so I do not bet on someone else's result
jobs.circumstance: at a dinner, a founder friend swears a mystery box stunt tripled their month; the founder wants to run it next week

progress.functional: our own read on a small group before a full launch
progress.emotional: stop betting on fear of missing out
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: copying the idea straight to the full list
jobs.fire: copying other brands' wins as if they were ours

forces.push: copied bets often flop because their buyers are not ours
forces.pull: a small test on 500 of our customers with a clear bar
forces.habit: if it worked for them, it will work for us
forces.anxiety: what if we miss the moment while we test

jobs.little_hire: each time an idea comes from another brand

watch.metric: borrowed ideas tested on a small group before full launch, per quarter
watch.source: brand brain (bet log)

drives.metric: share of bets that beat their read point bar

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a copied stunt lost $9,000. After: tested on 500 people first, dropped for $800.
jobs.not_for: a founder who never borrows ideas from other brands

jobs.job: When creators ask for free product, send it only to ones whose buyers match ours and count what each brings, so seeding is not a free giveaway
jobs.circumstance: 50 creators asked for product last month; 200 units went out and nobody knows what came back

progress.functional: a fit check before sending and orders counted per creator
